title: Armenia and Azerbaijan issue a joint statement on prisoner release and COP29
body:
Armenia and Azerbaijan issued a joint statement late on Thursday, 7 December 2023, saying they would pursue normalised relations and hoped to sign a peace treaty before the end of 2023. The agreement came from talks between the office of Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and the administration of Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev.

Azerbaijan said it would free 32 Armenian prisoners of war, and Armenia said it would release two Azerbaijani servicemen. Armenia also withdrew its own candidacy and backed Azerbaijan's bid to host the 29th UN climate conference, COP29, in 2024. A decision on the location and presidency of the meeting was due within the following week.

European Council President Charles Michel called the statement a major breakthrough in Armenia-Azerbaijan relations, and US State Department spokesman Matthew Miller described the prisoner exchange as an important confidence-building measure. The statement followed Azerbaijan's September 2023 offensive, after which most of Nagorno-Karabakh's roughly 120,000 ethnic Armenian residents fled.
